blocks.text: 46 תְּפִלָּה לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה 46
uncertainties: Running header. It is not prayer text.

blocks.text: אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ. יַעֲלֶה וְיָבֹא וְיַגִּיעַ וְיֵרָאֶה וְיֵרָצֶה וְיִשָּׁמַע וְיִפָּקֵד וְיִזָּכֵר זִכְרֹנֵנוּ וּפִקְדֹּנֵנוּ וְזִכְרוֹן אֲבוֹתֵינוּ. וְזִכְרוֹן מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן־דָּוִד עַבְדֶּךָ. וְזִכְרוֹן יְרוּשָׁלַיִם עִיר קָדְשֶׁךָ. וְזִכְרוֹן כָּל־עַמְּךָ בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל לְפָנֶיךָ. לִפְלֵטָה וּלְטוֹבָה וּלְחֵן וּלְחֶסֶד וּלְרַחֲמִים וּלְחַיִּים וּלְשָׁלוֹם בְּיוֹם הַזִּכָּרוֹן הַזֶּה. זָכְרֵנוּ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ בּוֹ לְטוֹבָה וּפָקְדֵנוּ בוֹ לִבְרָכָה וְהוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ בוֹ לְחַיִּים. וּבִדְבַר יְשׁוּעָה וְרַחֲמִים. חוּס וְחָנֵּנוּ. וְרַחֵם עָלֵינוּ וְהוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ. כִּי אֵלֶיךָ עֵינֵינוּ. כִּי אֵל מֶלֶךְ חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם אָתָּה:
uncertainties: זִכְרֹנֵנוּ: I read it defective, with no vav after the resh (holam on ר). Check whether a vav is there.
וּפִקְדֹּנֵנוּ: I read it defective, with no vav after the dalet. I can't tell whether the ד has a dagesh, and the holam may sit over the ד.
בּוֹ (first, after אֱלֹהֵינוּ): I can't tell whether the ב has a dagesh. I read the second and third בוֹ without one.
חוּס: I can't confirm the shuruq dot in the ו.
וְחָנֵּנוּ: I can't confirm the dagesh in the first נ.
וְיֵרָצֶה / וְיֵרָאֶה: I can't confirm the tsere under the yod at this resolution.

blocks.text: אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ. מְלוֹךְ עַל כָּל־הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ בִּכְבוֹדֶךָ וְהִנָּשֵׂא עַל כָּל־הָאָרֶץ בִּיקָרֶךָ וְהוֹפַע בַּהֲדַר גְּאוֹן עֻזֶּךָ עַל כָּל־יוֹשְׁבֵי תֵבֵל אַרְצֶךָ. וְיֵדַע כָּל־פָּעוּל כִּי אַתָּה פְּעַלְתּוֹ וְיָבִין כָּל־יָצוּר כִּי אַתָּה יְצַרְתּוֹ וְיֹאמַר כֹּל אֲשֶׁר נְשָׁמָה בְּאַפּוֹ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מֶלֶךְ וּמַלְכוּתוֹ בַּכֹּל מָשָׁלָה:
uncertainties: פְּעַלְתּוֹ: I can't tell whether the פ has a dagesh.
כֹּל (before אֲשֶׁר): it looks unpointed to me (כל). I can't confirm a holam or dagesh on the כ.
בְּאַפּוֹ: I can't confirm the dagesh in the ב or the פ.
תֵבֵל: I see no dagesh in the ת.
בַּכֹּל: I read a patah under the ב. I can't confirm the dagesh and holam on the כ.

blocks.text: בשבת
uncertainties: This is a small Rashi-script rubric inside the opening parenthesis. The glyphs look like two groups ('בש שבת'), so it could be an abbreviated form. I can't read it with confidence.

blocks.text: (בשבת אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ רְצֵה בִמְנוּחָתֵנוּ)
uncertainties: This is a Shabbat alternative. The parenthesis runs from the open bracket before the rubric to the close bracket after בִמְנוּחָתֵנוּ. On a weekday, leave out the whole span. On Shabbat, keep the words אֱלֹהֵינוּ … בִמְנוּחָתֵנוּ and drop the brackets and the rubric.
בִמְנוּחָתֵנוּ: I can't tell whether the ב has a dagesh.

blocks.text: קַדְּשֵׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתֶיךָ וְתֵן חֶלְקֵנוּ בְּתוֹרָתֶךָ שַׂבְּעֵנוּ מִטּוּבֶךָ וְשַׂמְּחֵנוּ בִּישׁוּעָתֶךָ.
uncertainties: מִטּוּבֶךָ: I can't confirm the dagesh in the ט.

blocks.text: בשבת
uncertainties: The same Rashi-script rubric as above. My reading is uncertain in the same way.

blocks.text: (בשבת וְהַנְחִילֵנוּ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ בְּאַהֲבָה וּבְרָצוֹן שַׁבַּת קָדְשֶׁךָ וְיָנוּחוּ בָהּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשֵׁי שְׁמֶךָ.)
uncertainties: This is a Shabbat alternative set in smaller type. It runs from the open bracket on the line ending בִּישׁוּעָתֶךָ to the close bracket after שְׁמֶךָ. The period is printed inside the bracket. On a weekday, leave out the whole span. On Shabbat, keep the words and drop the brackets and the rubric.
בָהּ: I can't confirm the mappiq in the ה.

blocks.text: וְטַהֵר לִבֵּנוּ לְעָבְדְּךָ בֶּאֱמֶת כִּי אַתָּה אֱלֹהִים אֱמֶת וּדְבָרְךָ (מלכנו) אֱמֶת וְקַיָּם לָעַד. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ מֶלֶךְ עַל כָּל־הָאָרֶץ מְקַדֵּשׁ (הַשַּׁבָּת וְ) יִשְׂרָאֵל וְיוֹם הַזִּכָּרוֹן:
uncertainties: (מלכנו) is printed small and unpointed in parentheses. It is a textual variant, not a Shabbat condition, and the English leaves it out.

(הַשַּׁבָּת וְ) is a Shabbat alternative. The close bracket comes right after the vav. On a weekday, leave out 'הַשַּׁבָּת וְ' and the brackets. On Shabbat, keep the words without the brackets, joined as 'הַשַּׁבָּת וְיִשְׂרָאֵל'.
לְעָבְדְּךָ: I read the second letter as having a qamats (qatan) and the ד as having a dagesh. I can't confirm either at this resolution.

blocks.text: רְצֵה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ בְּעַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל וּבִתְפִלָּתָם. וְהָשֵׁב אֶת הָעֲבוֹדָה לִדְבִיר בֵּיתֶךָ וְאִשֵּׁי יִשְׂרָאֵל וּתְפִלָּתָם בְּאַהֲבָה תְּקַבֵּל בְּרָצוֹן וּתְהִי לְרָצוֹן תָּמִיד עֲבוֹדַת יִשְׂרָאֵל עַמֶּךָ.
uncertainties: The page ends here, after עַמֶּךָ. The blessing continues on the next scan (s122), outside my assignment.
תְּקַבֵּל: I can't confirm the dagesh in the initial ת.
וְאִשֵּׁי: I can't confirm the dagesh in the ש.

blocks.text: 46 Morning Prayer for the New Year 46
uncertainties: Running header. It is not prayer text.

blocks.text: אלהינו

Our God and God of our fathers, may there rise and come and arrive and appear and be favourably received and be heard and considered and remain in memory before Thee, our remembrance and our consideration and the memory of our fathers and the memory of the anointed, the son of David, Thy servant, and the memory of Jerusalem the Holy City, and the memory of all Thy people, the House of Israel, for deliverance and for happiness, for favour and for grace and for compassion, for life and for peace on this Day of Remembrance. Remember us, O Lord our God, on it for happiness, consider us on it for blessing and help us on it unto life, and through the word of salvation and compassion, spare us and be gracious unto us have compassion upon us, and help us, for towards Thee our eyes are turned, for Thou O God, art a gracious and merciful King.
uncertainties: 'mem-/ory' is a line-end hyphen, rejoined as 'memory'.
A comma seems to be missing after 'gracious unto us'. I left it as printed.

blocks.text: א״א
uncertainties: Printed as 'א״א', an abbreviation for אלהינו ואלהי אבותינו.

blocks.text: Our God and God of our fathers, reign over the whole world in Thy glory and rise above the whole earth in Thy grandeur. Shine forth in the exalted beauty of Thy might upon all the inhabitants of the territory of Thine earth so that every creature may recognize that Thou hast created it and that every form may understand that Thou hast formed it and all with breath in the nostrils may say: The Lord, the God of Israel, is King and His Kingdom rules over all.
uncertainties: In the first 'fathers' the h glyph is damaged in print. The word is still clear.

blocks.text: (Our God and God of our fathers, take pleasure in our rest.)
uncertainties: This is a Shabbat alternative. The whole span, brackets included, is suppressed on a weekday. On Shabbat, drop the brackets; the period is inside the close bracket. There is no English rubric.

blocks.text: Sanctify us through Thy commandments and grant our portion in Thy Torah, satisfy us with Thy goodness and gladden us with Thy help
(and grant us, O Lord our God, in love and favour, Thy holy Sabbath as a portion so that Israel, who sanctifies Thy Name, may rest on it)
uncertainties: This is a Shabbat alternative running from '(and grant' to 'on it)'. On a weekday, suppress it together with its brackets. The English has no period inside the brackets, but the Hebrew does.

blocks.text: and purify our heart to serve Thee in truth for Thou, O Lord, art truth and Thy word is truth and endures for ever. Blessed art Thou, O Lord King over the whole earth, who sanctifies (the Sabbath and) Israel and the Day of Remembrance.
uncertainties: '(the Sabbath and)' is a Shabbat alternative. On a weekday, suppress the span with its brackets. On Shabbat, keep the words without the brackets.
There is no comma after 'O Lord' in 'O Lord King'. I left it as printed.
The English has nothing for the Hebrew variant (מלכנו).

blocks.text: רצה

Take delight, O Lord our God, in Thy people Israel and in their prayer and restore the service to the sanctuary of Thy House and accept with love and favour the fire offerings of Israel and their prayer, and may the service of Thy people Israel be a perpetual delight.
uncertainties: The page ends here. The blessing continues on the next scan (s122).

notes: I transcribed only scans s120 and s121. Both carry printed page 46.
In the enlarged bands the top of s120-band2 and s120-band3 repeats the last line of the band above it. I counted each line once.
I found no Biblical citations, cantillation or speaker sigla on these pages. All the text is liturgical, with vowel points only.
There are no Rashi-script rubrics other than the two small 'בשבת'-type labels at the start of the Shabbat parentheses. Their exact glyphs are uncertain.

Possible corrections: (1) English, add a comma after 'gracious unto us'. (2) English, add a comma after 'O Lord' in 'O Lord King'. (3) Hebrew, check the defective spellings זִכְרֹנֵנוּ and וּפִקְדֹּנֵנוּ against the page image. I kept them as I read them and did not normalize them.

On the vowels: at this resolution I can't confirm every dagesh or holam point in the small type. I listed the specific doubtful words and letters for each block. A higher-resolution check of the Shabbat parentheses and the חתימה line is recommended.
